Dear Mr. Rehma:
This office has reviewed the proposed draft environmental statement of the Proposed Endangered Species Conservation Act of 1972 prepared by the Bureau of Sport Pisheries and Wildlife of the Department of Interior. Our comments are as follows:
1. We seriously question the propriety of preparing a draft statement covering general legislation of the magnitude and scope contained in the Enlangered Species Conservation Act of 1972. If this approach is acceptable in an error covering as many decisions as can be expected from the Administration of this Act, why is it not permissible and acceptable for other federal agencies to prepare statements covering their organic actions without consideration of each individual action taken under such authority.
2. In considering and discussing alternates, it is notable that a proposal for "no action" was not discussed.
3. It is our recommendation that the Bureau of Sport Fisheries and Wildlife or such other federal agency as may now administer the provisions of this act be required to prepare a complete environmental impact statement for each program proposed to affect an endangered species as the species are identified and that the statement include consideration of the effect of the act as it relates to the human race.
Sincerely,
chirond L. Summers
Acting Executive Director
